# First Chapter
<meta>continues from previous page: ...as suffering, as self-less. By doing so, he attains clarity and recognizes the vanity of his desire.</meta>

As it is said in the *Āryaratnakūṭasūtra* <gloss>Noble Heap of Jewels Sutra</gloss>. Then, those five hundred monks, not comprehending, not penetrating, and not having faith in the teaching of the Dharma <gloss>truth/doctrine</gloss> of the Blessed One, rose from their seats and departed. Then the Blessed One created two monks on the path by which those monks were traveling.

Then those five hundred monks approached the path where those two monks—who were *nirmitaka* <gloss>magically created beings</gloss>—were traveling. Having approached, they said to them: "Where are you going, venerable ones?" The created ones replied: "We shall go to the forest dwellings; there we shall dwell in the happiness of meditative contact <gloss>states of deep trance</gloss>. For the Dharma that the Blessed One teaches, we do not comprehend, we do not penetrate, we do not have faith in; we become agitated, we experience distress." Then those five hundred monks said: "We also, venerable ones, do not comprehend, do not penetrate, do not have faith in the teaching of the Dharma of the Blessed One; we become agitated, we experience distress. Therefore, we shall dwell in the forest dwellings in the happiness of meditative contact." The created ones replied: "In that case, venerable ones, we shall live together; we shall not dispute. For the Dharma of a *śramaṇa* <gloss>ascetic/monk</gloss> is supreme in non-dispute." <unclear>******</unclear> "For the abandonment of what, venerable ones, have you undertaken this path?" They replied: "For the abandonment of attachment, aversion, and delusion, we have undertaken..."

<note>1) Tibetan: "From the *dKon mchog brtsegs pa* <gloss>Ratnakūṭa</gloss>" — See the same text cited below ad XVII. 33.</note>

<note>2) The Tibetan adds "having attained *dhyāna* <gloss>meditation</gloss>," cf. *Kathāvatthu* a. 38. 8.</note>

<note>3) The words in parentheses are according to the Tibetan and the citation ad XVII. 33. — *nirmitaka* <gloss>created being</gloss>, *Prajñāpāramitā* 442. 14.</note>

<note>4) *sukhasparçaṃ viharati* <gloss>dwells in comfortable contact</gloss>, see *Mahāvyutpatti* 245. 649, 255. 3. 5 and *Śikṣāsamuccaya* 200. 18 where M. Bendall points to *Lalitavistara* 357. 12 and *Mahāvastu* I. 623.</note>

<note>5) *avivāda* <gloss>non-dispute</gloss>. Compare *Śikṣāsamuccaya* 263. 18: "What one does not dispute is in accordance with the duty of an ascetic" (cf. 195. 7, 281. 14) — *Mahāvyutpatti* 245. 1189 — *Lotus Sutra*, XIV. 33: "I am to utter an infallible word; refrain from disputing (vivāda, replaced in the manuscript by viṣāda <gloss>sadness</gloss>) about it: the science of the Tathāgata is beyond reasoning." — *avivāda* = *ācāra* <gloss>conduct</gloss> defined in the *Sarvadarśanasaṅgraha* (15. 11): "Acceptance of the words of the teacher." — The six *vivādamūlas* <gloss>roots of dispute</gloss>, *Majjhima Nikāya* II. 245. — "Everyone disputes, except the monks," *ibid.* p. 120.</note>

<note>6) Cf. below folio 100a. Our text is abbreviated.</note>

<summary>This page recounts an episode from the Ratnakūṭa Sutra where a group of monks, unable to understand the Buddha's teachings, encounter two magically created monks who advocate for meditative withdrawal and the abandonment of mental afflictions to avoid dispute.</summary>
<keywords>Ratnakūṭasūtra, Dharma, nirmitaka, dhyāna, śramaṇa, avivāda, mental afflictions</keywords>
